declared.title: Entry through the narrow door: The costs of just failing high stakes exams
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « Machin McNally Ruiz-Valenzuela entry through the narrow door English exam threshold » (2026-11-26); named by the counter-evidence review

population: students in England sitting a high-stakes national exam at the end of compulsory schooling: just below vs just above the pass mark, followed to age 18-19

findings.text: Three years later, students who just failed the exam were less likely to enter a high-level academic or vocational track and to start higher education

support.sentence: Three years later, students who just fail to achieve the required threshold have a lower probability of entering an upper-secondary high-level academic or vocational track and of starting tertiary education.

findings.text: Students who just failed were also more likely to have left education by 18 without a job

support.sentence: Those who fail to pass the threshold are also more likely to drop out of education by age 18, without some form of employment.

limits: quasi-experiment around a pass mark (regression discontinuity, regraded marks), not random assignment
the pass mark opens doors (tracks, courses): the cost of failing is partly closed doors, not what failing taught
one exam in England; sample size not given in the abstract (administrative data); abstract read from OpenAlex only
